# The Šw file: from shu to the temple it became
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Šw** is what the evidence put back.

Shu's mythology is cosmogony in motion. He is not a hero who goes on quests; he is the first differentiation of the creator, the void that becomes space, the breath that makes the world inhabitable. Without him, Nut and Geb would remain locked together and no life could arise. In Pyramid Text Utterance 600, Atum stands on the primeval mound and 'sneezes Shu, spits Tefnut'.  The wordplay is precise: Shu's name resembles the word for sneeze, Tefnut's for spit.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Šw
- **ASCII form:** shu
- **Meaning:** "Emptiness, he who rises up"
- **Domain of influence:** Air, Wind, Lions
- **Pantheon:** Egyptian
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𓄑
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 223 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

**Šw** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *shu* and **Šw** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Šw** lives at [/sites/shu/](/sites/shu/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/shu/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/shu/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/shu/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Šw** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Wind & Atmospheric Energy** — He holds the sky apart from the earth and fills the space between with moving air — Egypt’s wind and breath made god.
- **Aviation & Aerospace** — Air and wind personified, the lift beneath the wing.
- **Environmental & Climate Services** — The atmosphere personified — the fragile, life-sustaining layer the sector exists to monitor.

If a match here reads wrong, the atlas says how to challenge it. The patterns are falsifiable — that is what makes them worth publishing.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Egyptian tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [The Book of the Dead](/texts/book-of-the-dead/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/shu/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Śiva** ([read it here](/sites/shiva/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **sjꜣ** ([read it here](/sites/sia/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
